# Test fixtures (real media)

Regenerate with `node scripts/make-fixtures.mjs` (downloads pinned sdists, verifies SHA-256, extracts files, and
generates media with the project's own ffmpeg.wasm and Chromium). Used only by tests — never shipped in the site.

  circular, a restaurant bill, and a leaflet, a medicine leaflet in small print with a list, a café's menu with dot leaders and a letter
  (Camera Reader) of our own making (no real product's or company's design; names, numbers and addresses made
  up), "photographed" on a desk — perspective, a shadow, light falling off, blur, noise, JPEG; one label photographed with the phone
  held sideways, one carrying a Wi-Fi QR code; the cards (28 Nov 2026: eight) — one with a vCard QR code, one from the United States,
  a dark one, a card's front and back. truth.json holds what each says.

## deadlines/
- `reference.json` — dates as papers write them (numbers day first and month first, words, weekdays, ordinals, no year) read by Python's
  dateutil, and dates counted on (relativedelta, timedelta): the reference of `tests/unit/deadlines.test.mjs`, made by `python3
  scripts/make-deadlines-reference.py` (needs `pip install python-dateutil`).

## spell/
- `reference.json` — misspellings with the suggestions native Hunspell 1.7.6 gives (built from the same source as hunspell.wasm,
  `wasm/hunspell/build.sh`) and the order the tab gives them (checked against a second reading of the rules in Python); the words each
  dictionary must take or refuse; the measured share of right words first. Made by `python3 scripts/make-spell-reference.py`. The
  misspellings are a part of codespell 2.4.1's `dictionary.txt` (GPL-2.0, github.com/codespell-project/codespell — from Wikipedia's lists
  of common misspellings) and our list of classic misspellings.

## worldclock/
- `reference.json` — astral 3.2's sunrise and sunset (seconds since 1970, or "up" / "down" / null) for 161 cities of
  `src/lib/worldcities.json` on 49 days of 2026 – 2027, and every change of UTC offset in 2026 – 2027 of 357 zones as Python's zoneinfo
  gives it over the system's tzdata (2026e): the reference of `tests/unit/worldclock.test.mjs`, made by `python3
  scripts/make-worldclock-reference.py` (needs `pip install astral==3.2`). Made by us; free to use.
- `ids.json` — every city's id, name and coordinates as `scripts/make-worldclock-cities.py` makes them (GeoNames' data, CC BY 4.0, via
  geonamescache 3.0.2): the unit suite makes the ids again in TypeScript.

## vector/
- `logo.png` (640 × 400: a red disc in a black ring, a blue rounded square with a white bar, a yellow triangle, on white — drawn at 4× and made
  smaller), `signature.jpg` (640 × 300: a signature in blue ink photographed on paper lit unevenly, a shadow at a corner, a camera's noise, JPEG
  at 85) with `signature-mask.png` (the ink as it was drawn), `pixel.png` (24 × 24 pixel art in six colours), `truth.json` (their colours and
  sizes) — made by `python3 scripts/make-vector-fixtures.py` (Pillow, numpy; a fixed seed). Made by us; free to use. Image to SVG's pictures.
- `u2net-chelsea.png`, `u2net-astronaut.png`, `u2net-coffee.png` — U²-Net small's 320 × 320 masks of `images/chelsea.png`, `astronaut.png`
  and `coffee.png` made by rembg's own steps in Python on ONNX Runtime (`python3 scripts/make-u2net-reference.py`; needs onnxruntime, Pillow,
  numpy and the model fetched by `npm run assets`): the reference of the Clipart Maker's cut-out in `tests/unit/vector.test.mjs`.

## diagram/
- `media.vsdx` — a Visio drawing of six shapes (a rectangle, a circle, a line, straight and curved connectors, a connected shape, each named
  in its text) made with Microsoft Visio: the template that the Python package vsdx 0.6.1 carries (`vsdx/media/media.vsdx` of its source
  on PyPI; BSD-3-Clause, © 2020 Dave Howard). The Diagram Editor's Visio file (`tests/e2e/diagram.e2e.mjs`).
- `flow.drawio`, `flow.drawio.png`, `flow.drawio.svg` — a small flowchart (two shapes and a labelled connector) saved by draw.io 32.7.7 in
  the Diagram Editor tab with its Save, PNG and SVG (`node scripts/make-diagram-fixtures.mjs` after `npm run build`): the files
  `tests/unit/diagram.test.mjs` reads the diagram out of. Made by us; free to use.

## radio/ (World Radio)
- `stations.json`, `countries.json`, `languages.json`, `tags.json` — answers of Radio Browser's API (radio-browser.info: an open,
  community-run directory), recorded on 28 Nov 2026 by `python3 scripts/make-radio-fixtures.py` and cut down to the fields World Radio
  reads (no logos): 305 stations — India's most listened, All India Radio's, the quick picks' genres, the world's most listened —, the
  countries, the 300 languages and genres with the most stations. The e2e harness answers every page's requests to the directory from
  them (`tests/lib/radiostub.mjs`), so no suite reaches the real one; the unit suite reads stations from them.
- `tone.mp3` (440 Hz, 40 s), `short.mp3` (880 Hz, 2 s) and `hls/` (an HLS stream: 660 Hz, 24 s in MPEG-TS pieces of 4 s) — test streams
  made with ffmpeg (sine tones; made by us, free to use): what the World Radio suite's stand-in station servers send.

## wallpapers/ (Wallpapers)
- `feed.json` — Wikipedia's featured feed of 28 Nov 2026 (`en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/feed/featured/2026/11/28`), cut to its Picture of
  the Day: "Lower Manhattan from Jersey City November 2014 panorama 3" by King of Hearts (CC BY-SA 3.0; the description's text is Wikimedia
  Commons', CC BY-SA). Recorded by `python3 scripts/make-wallpaper-fixtures.py --feed FILE`.
- `commons-search.json` — an answer of Commons' search among its featured pictures in the format of MediaWiki's action API (formatversion 2,
  pages by id with their rank in `index`), **written by the script from the feed's real Picture of the Day** (its file, size, author, licence
  and description): Commons' API — and, after one answer, the feed — refused the recording machine (HTTP 429, Wikimedia's rate limit), so
  their own answers could not be recorded.
- `met-search.json`, `met-highlights.json`, `met-objects.json` — the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access API (v1.1 search for landscape
  paintings, its highlights; the 18 objects they name, cut to the fields the tab reads), recorded on 28 Nov 2026; the Met's data is CC0.
- `aic-search.json`, `aic-boosted.json` — the Art Institute of Chicago's API (public-domain landscape paintings; its highlighted "boosted"
  ones), recorded on 28 Nov 2026; its data CC0, the `short_description` texts CC BY 4.0 (Art Institute of Chicago).
- `busy.jpg` (1600 × 1000: a gradient with a checkered block at x 1150 – 1450, y 300 – 700), `face.jpg` (1600 × 600: the astronaut's
  portrait of `images/astronaut.png` — NASA, public domain — at the right of a plain picture) and `tall.jpg` (600 × 1200, a checkered block
  at x 150 – 450, y 800 – 1000) — test pictures made by the script (made by us, free to use): what the stand-in picture servers send
  (`tests/lib/wallstub.mjs`), the e2e harness answering every page's requests to the services from these files.

## nasa/ (NASA Image Explorer)
- `search-earth.json`, `search-earth-2.json`, `search-nebula.json`, `search-apollo.json`, `search-video.json` — answers of NASA's Image and Video
  Library API (`images-api.nasa.gov/search`: "earth from space" pages 1 and 2, "nebula", "apollo 11" in 1969, "mars rover" videos), and
  `assets.json` — its file lists (`/asset/<id>`) of four items; recorded on 28 Nov 2026 by `python3 scripts/make-nasa-fixtures.py`. NASA's data and
  descriptions are NASA's (not copyrighted in the United States; some items name other parties in their credits, as recorded). The e2e harness
  answers every page's requests to NASA from them (`tests/lib/nasastub.mjs`), with the Wallpapers' test pictures for NASA's pictures and
  `media/clip.mp4`, `media/subs.srt` for its videos and captions.

## stitch/ (Long Screenshot Stitcher)
- Phone screenshots of our own making, by `python3 scripts/make-stitch-shots.py` (Noto Sans, OFL; every chat, page, name and number made up — a
  chat in the manner of a messaging app, a news page in the manner of a newspaper's, no real app's or site's design): `chat-1` … `chat-5.png` (a
  chat scrolled down, 720 × 1600: a wallpaper that stays put, the clock and the contact's line changing, a date chip and a scroll-down button
  floating, a scrollbar's thumb), `chatdark-*.png` (the dark theme), `chatsent-*.jpg` (the chat on a 1080 × 2400 phone, sent through a chat app:
  two thirds the size, JPEG 75), `web-*.png` and `webjpeg-*.jpg` (a news page in a phone's browser: the address bar in the first screenshot only, a
  site header and a cookie banner that stay), `small-*`, `large-*` (a sliver and nine tenths in common), `repeat-*` (runs of the same "Ok"),
  `mix-*` (the chat's first four, the third sent as a 480-px JPEG), `IMG_2038` … `IMG_2044.png` (the chat's under other names, a duplicate and a
  page of something else). `truth.json`: for each screenshot the page row its row y shows (y + offset), the part that scrolls, what floats over it;
  each set's order top to bottom.
- `finder/` — the Screenshot Finder's test pictures, made by `python3 scripts/make-finder-shots.py` (needs pillow and pillow-heif; Noto Sans, OFL): a
  phone's screenshots of our own making, in the manner of such apps (no real app's design) — a chat about a train booking
  (`Screenshot_20261102-190712_WhatsApp.png`), a dark-mode chat with a Wi-Fi password, a bank's SMS with an OTP, an order e-mail, the phone's
  "About phone", a payment —, a PC's screenshot of a booking page (`Screenshot 2026-11-03 at 10.12.44.png`), an iPhone's HEIC (`IMG_4471.HEIC`, a
  boarding pass), and photos: the camera helpers' school circular and restaurant bill (copies of `snaps/notice-school.jpg`, `snaps/restaurant.jpg`)
  and the coffee photo without text (`images/coffee.jpg`). Every name, number and page is made up. `truth.json`: the words each picture must give,
  queries with the pictures they find in the tab's order, the pictures without text, every text drawn on each screenshot and where each word was
  drawn (`boxes`: word, x0, y0, x1, y1 in the picture's pixels).
- `realcheck/` — the test pictures of Is This Screenshot Real?, made by `python3 scripts/make-realcheck-shots.py` (needs pillow and numpy, and the
  native exiftool — `apt install libimage-exiftool-perl` — for the thumbnail's EXIF; Noto Sans, OFL): a payment receipt of a made-up UPI app ("Kaveri
  Pay" — no real app's design; every name and number made up) as a phone's screenshot (`receipt-genuine.png`), as it arrives after a chat app sent
  it (`IMG-20261106-WA0007.jpg`: smaller, JPEG at quality 78, no metadata), and doctored: the amount repainted after that JPEG and saved again at 92
  (`receipt-edited.jpg`) or saved as a PNG (`receipt-sent.png`), repainted and saved by "Adobe Photoshop" (`receipt-photoshop.png`: its Software tag
  and XMP history), repainted with a thumbnail that still shows the old amount and a later modify date (`receipt-thumb.jpg`, "Snapseed"), and a
  receipt that says what none can (`receipt-impossible.png`: its clock before the payment, a weekday not the date's, an 11-digit reference, two
  amounts); photos — the astronaut (`images/astronaut.png`, public domain, NASA) with its mission patch hidden under fabric copied from the suit
  (`photo-cloned.jpg`, and stored on its side with EXIF orientation 6: `photo-cloned-turned.jpg`), a greyscale JPEG of it (`grey.jpg`), and Pillow's
  `flower.jpg` (`photo-camera.jpg`: a Canon camera's JPEG with its own thumbnail, nothing edited; Pillow, MIT-CMU); `coefs-base.jpg` /
  `coefs-prog.jpg` — one set of pixels saved baseline and progressive at one quality (the same coefficients). `testorig.jpg` and `testimgari.jpg` —
  libjpeg-turbo 3.1.3's own test pictures (`testimages/`, IJG licence): one picture as a baseline and an arithmetic-coded JPEG. `truth.json`: each
  picture's signs, the areas edited, the qualities it was saved at. The measuring set (`python3 scripts/make-realcheck-eval.py OUT`, 647 files) is
  made on demand and not committed.
